_note: Climate calendars (docs/WORLD-REGIONS.md §7, §11). One template per climate family. seasons[]: in year order from world day-of-year 0; days add to 365; each weather table sums to 1 (clear/rain/cold have effects today; heat/storm are rolled and stored only). months[12]: the season for each real month Jan..Dec, NORTHERN-hemisphere frame; a southern region reads it six months on (its July is the template's January). Each season must be one unbroken run of months, in the same order as seasons[]. A region uses climate.calendar (or familyCalendar[climateFamily]); its own climate.seasons, if any, replace the template's seasons; its own climate.months, if any, is literal (no hemisphere shift). Steve 2026-10-14: 'Yes that's okay to run a wet/dry year. Whenever the player starts, should be the season the game starts in.'

Harvest. Nuts, last greens. Fatten up.
The boss. Stored food or nothing.
Blizzards with nothing to stop them.
Everything flowers at once, then dries.

Rivers drop. Fish crowd the pools.

talk._note: WHERE ARE WE (src/js/whereAreWe.js). What a villager says when asked where we are / what season it is. It depends on THEIR familiarity with the landing region (Game.familiarityTier of their origin): local -> they know (player learns it, level 2); visitor -> a rough guess (level 1, the season may be one off near a boundary); stranger -> they don't know (no change). Lines resolve most specific first: calendars[calendarId].seasons[id] -> seasons[id]; regions[id].local -> regionLocal; families[climateFamily] -> familyDefault. Slots: {region}/{Region} (display name), {rough}/{Rough} (the family's rough description). A tier-2 line must name the truth. Muse: add regional voice here, not in code. Steve 2026-10-14: 'Okay add season line but that's a small knowledge unlock as you speak to people. Where we are in the world becomes part of conversation.'
askLabels: "What season is it here, do you think?"

known: "Spring. Early greens are up. The hungry season's ending."
"Spring. The sap's moving. Anyone from here knows that smell."
guess: "Feels like spring to me. Could be wrong."

known: "Summer. Berries soon, and storms with them."
late: "Summer's wearing out. Fall's coming. Get the nuts in."

known: "Fall. Leaves are turning. That's the harvest clock."
"Autumn. Nuts are dropping. Fatten up while you can."
late: "Late fall. Winter's coming, and it's long here."

known: "Winter. Stored food or nothing, that's how it goes here."
"Deep winter. Nothing grows till the thaw."
late: "Winter's back is broken. The thaw's close."
guess: "Winter, or near it. My bones say so."

known: "The cool season. The kind days. Use them."
late: "The cool's almost done. The heat comes next."
guess: "The cool time, I think. It'll get hotter."

known: "The hot season. Work early, rest at noon."
late: "The heat breaks soon. Not soon enough."
guess: "Hot season, I'd guess. Feels like it."

known: "The dry. Water first, everything else after."
late: "End of the dry. The wet's coming, you can smell it."
guess: "Dry season, I think. Somewhere in it."
"The rains? Feels like the wet to me."

known: "The cool dry. Herds walk to water."
late: "The cool dry's ending. Hot and dry next."
guess: "Cool and dry. That season, I'd say."

known: "The hot dry. Before the rains break."
late: "Hot dry's nearly done. The wet's coming."
guess: "The hot dry, maybe. Hard to say."

regionLocal: "{Region}. I grew up with country like this."

na_eastern_woodlands.name: Eastern Woodlands
local: "These are the eastern woods. Oak, hickory, creeks. I grew up two valleys from trees like these."
"The Eastern Woodlands. Same oaks I climbed as a kid. They dropped me home."
"These are beech woods. Oak, beech, hornbeam — I grew up picking mushrooms under trees like these."
"Temperate Europe. The forest gives, but you have to know what you're looking at. Half of it will kill you."
"Home woods. Mast in the fall, mushrooms after rain, and the hungry gap in March. You learn the gap or the gap learns you."
eu_temperate.name: Temperate Europe

local: "A Amazônia. The river decides everything here — where you walk, what you eat, when you sleep."
"You hear it before you see it: at night the forest is louder than any city I ever knew."
"Manaus is that way — or it was. The forest doesn't care about directions anymore."
"Don't drink the river straight. Nobody who grew up here ever did."
sa_amazon.name: The Amazon

local: "The Sahel. Baobab country — you can tell by the upside-down trees. I grew up not far from land like this."
"Home ground, almost. The rains come, the millet grows, the dry takes it back. We know this dance."
"The savanna. Watch the waterholes at dusk — everything drinks, including the lions."
"This is my country. Pearl millet in the rains, hungry season after. Stay near the baobabs; they mark the old villages."
africa_sahel_savanna.name: Sahel and the Savanna

local: "This is home. Mango trees, monsoon rain, heat that sits on your chest. You can smell the wet earth before the clouds even break."
"South Asia. My grandmother's village had a banyan like that one. Watch the rivers in the wet season — they don't ask permission."
"Delhi heat in May, Bengal rain in July. This land doesn't do anything halfway, stranger."
"Rice country. The paddies feed everyone if the rains come on time. Pray they come on time."
south_asia.name: South Asia

local: "East Asia. Bamboo, paddies, persimmon trees. I'd know these hills anywhere."
"Home. The plum rains come soon — you can smell it in the air already."
"They dropped me in East Asia. Chestnut lanes, feral paddies, cranes on the wetlands. I grew up two valleys from country like this."
"East Asia, and not the postcard version. Watch the ditches in summer — the water takes what it wants."
east_asia.name: East Asia

visitor: "Somewhere with big woods and real winters. Like home, but the trees are wrong."
"Four seasons, broadleaf woods. Not my woods though."
"Open grass country. Could be a lot of places."
"Somewhere warm with dry summers. South, maybe."
"Far north. Pine and long dark. Not my north though."
"Desert country. I know dry when I feel it. Not which dry."
"Savanna, somewhere hot. The grass tells me that much."
"Somewhere warm, south maybe. Rain like this I know."
"Monsoon country. I'd bet on that, not on where."
"High up. Thin air. Somewhere in the mountains."
"Warm, dry scrub. Somewhere south, I think."

stranger: "Where are we? I couldn't tell you. Nothing here grows where I'm from."
"Your guess is as good as mine. The sky's the same, that's all I know."
"Don't ask me. I'm still learning which way the sun sets here."
